channel.title: AGSIST Daily
channel.description: Free morning market briefing for grain and livestock farmers: overnight futures, USDA reports and the news behind the moves. Posted most days between 5:45 and 6:30 a.m. Central, by Sigurd Lindquist, CCA.

item.title: Corn down 6 straight days to $4.59½; beans down 7 to $12.45
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn closed Tuesday at $4.59½, its sixth lower close in a row, and soybeans at $12.45 made it seven. A corn bushel is worth about 15 cents less than a week ago. Harvest is pushing the selling, and nothing new came overnight. • Grains keep sliding on harvest • Cattle and hogs firm; crude near $100 Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-21

item.title: Corn at $4.67¾ and beans at $12.57½ barely move after losing streaks
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn at $4.67¾ and soybeans at $12.57½ are both a few cents higher overnight, which is hardly a bounce after streaks of five and six lower closes. A farmer holding unpriced bushels is still looking at the lowest prices of the run. • Grains bounce after losing runs • Crude slips but stays above $100 Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-20

item.title: Crude down 3% to $98.41 on Trump-Putin diesel deal; grains flat
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Crude fell about $3 overnight to **$98.41** on word of a US-Russia deal that could add diesel supply. Corn at **$4.73** and beans at **$12.61** barely noticed. For harvest fuel bills, that is the first bit of relief in a while, though crude is still close to $100. • Crude slips on diesel deal • Grains hold flat • Cattle edged up Friday Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-19

item.title: Corn slips 3¾¢ to $4.74¼; crude gains 3.5% to $101
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn closed Friday at $4.74¼, down 3¾ cents, while soybeans held at $12.61¼ and wheat lost 9½ cents. Crude was the big mover, up 3.5% to $101.41 as Iran war supply worries carry into 2027. • Grains ease into the weekend • Cattle firm, packers in focus Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-18

item.title: Corn and beans break lower; crude tops $101 on tight supply
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn settled Friday at $4.74¼, down 3¾ cents, and beans closed at $12.61¼, off 1¾ cents, both pressured by harvest supply all week. Crude gained 3.5% to $101.41 after the IEA pushed emergency stock releases and the US offered another 17 million barrels from the reserve. • Corn and beans ease into the weekend • Cattle firm on cash hopes • Crude tops $101 on tight supply Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-17

item.title: Corn and beans break lower as harvest pressure builds
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn is at $4.74¼ overnight, down 4 cents, and beans are off 3¾ cents at $12.60½. China bought more US beans this week, its first cargoes since the Trump-Xi summit, but harvest supply is still winning. Every bushel coming out of the field right now is being sold into a market that already has plenty. • Corn and beans break lower • Cattle firm, feeders hold • Crude holds near $99 on tanker risk Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-16

item.title: Grain holds steady overnight ahead of export sales report
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn is trading at $4.80 overnight, barely off Wednesday's $4.80¾ settle. Beans sit at $12.73¼, down 4 cents, with weekly export sales due Thursday at 7:30 a.m. CT. Nothing has moved yet, so the board is sitting right where harvest left it. • Corn and beans wait on export sales • Cattle and hogs ease back slightly • Crude slips as Trump weighs easing tanker sanctions Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-15

item.title: Crude tops $95 on more tanker threats; grain holds steady
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: WTI crude is at $95.36 overnight, up 1.3%, after Iran told Reuters its forces plan to intensify strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Corn and wheat drifted lower overnight while beans firmed to $12.90½. Diesel costs for fall fieldwork are the thing to watch, not the grain board. • Corn and wheat drift, beans firm • Crude pushes toward $95 on Hormuz threats Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-14

item.title: Corn and beans drift lower as crop progress looms
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn settled Monday at $4.83 and sits at $4.81¼ overnight, down less than two cents, while beans are off almost a nickel at $12.83. Both markets are flat because USDA's record crop numbers are already priced in, not because anyone expects news today. • Grain finds its footing • Cattle and hogs mixed overnight • Crude pulls back from Saudi move higher Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-13

item.title: Corn steadies near $4.81 after Friday's WASDE hit
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn is at $4.81 overnight, up 1¼¢ from Friday's $4.79¾ settle, a small bounce after Friday's near 4% drop on USDA's yield number. Soybean meal gained 2.2% to $368.70 while beans slipped to $12.83. Monday's quiet bounce doesn't undo Friday's loss on unpriced corn. • Corn finds its feet after WASDE • Cattle and feeders keep climbing • Crude firms as tankers take more hits Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-12

item.title: Corn's 4.1% WASDE drop closes out a mixed week
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn settled Friday at $4.80, down 4.1% after WASDE came in heavier than the trade wanted. Cattle shrugged it off, closing the week at $224.60, up 1.2%, with feeders up 1.7% to $343.90. Every bushel of old-crop corn sitting in the bin is worth about 19 cents less than it was Thursday. • Corn takes the brunt of wasde • Cattle and feeders close the week firm • Diesel politics move to the front Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-11

item.title: Corn drops 4.1% Friday on WASDE; cattle hold the gains
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn settled at $4.80 Friday, down almost 20 cents, after WASDE numbers came in heavier than the trade wanted. Cattle didn't blink, closing at $224.60, up 1.2% on the week. Every bushel still in the bin is worth less than it was Thursday morning. • Corn takes the WASDE hit • Cattle and feeders close the week strong Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-10

item.title: Crude pulls back from the Hormuz run as grains sit quiet
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn is at $5.01 overnight, basically flat, holding the line it has worked to defend since getting back over $5 on Monday. Crude eased 1.0% to $90.60 after a 4.9% run Wednesday, with Brent still above $100 on Hormuz tanker disruptions, ongoing since July and flaring again this week. • Corn holds the round number again • Beans firm, meal leads the complex • Crude gives a little back Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-09

item.title: Crude runs 5% on Hormuz, soy oil breaks hard
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: WTI's at $92.61 overnight, up 4.9% after another tanker took fire off Qatar, the first deep-Gulf hit since fighting flared there back in September. Soybean oil got hit the other way, down 3.1% as meal took over the complex's weight. That split already moved crush margins before a single export sales number hit the tape. • Crude Runs On Fresh Tanker Hit • Soy Oil Breaks, Meal Takes Over • Corn Grinds At The Round Number Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-08

item.title: Cattle jump on feeder strength as corn slips back
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Live cattle are trading at $221.23 overnight, up 1.8%, with feeders up 2.0% to $340.50, both printing well above Tuesday's settle with no fresh Cattle on Feed data behind it. Corn slipped back to $5.04, giving up the round number it just reclaimed Monday as rain-stalled harvest meets heavy Grain Stocks. • Cattle And Feeders Both Jump • Corn Slips Back Under $5.08 Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-07

item.title: Corn holds $5 as grain stocks come in heavy
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn traded at $5.00 overnight, up 3 cents from Monday's $4.97¼ settle, even after USDA's Grain Stocks report put old-crop corn bushels at 2.10 billion, up 35% from a year ago. Soybeans added a nickel to $12.86 on a 3% stocks draw the other direction. • Corn Shrugs Off Heavy Stocks • Beans Firm On Tighter Stocks • Cattle Soft, Crude Breaks Lower Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-06

item.title: Corn back above $5 as rain keeps combines parked
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn closed $5.00, up 4 and a quarter cents, clawing back the round number it lost Friday while El Nino rain keeps the Belt's combines sitting in the shed. Soybean oil ran 2.7% on the back of soymeal's firm tone, the two products pulling in the same direction for once. • Corn Reclaims The Round Number • Soy Complex Leads On Products • Cattle Soft, Feeders Give More Back Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-05

item.title: Corn closes under $5 with harvest stuck in the rain
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn settled Friday at $4.97, soybeans at $12.77, both down 20 to 40 cents on the week by the wire's own math. Record El Nino rain has stalled harvest across the Corn Belt at the exact moment farmers need combines rolling and bins filling. • Grains Grind Lower Into Harvest • Cattle Soft, Hogs Firm Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-04

item.title: Crude splits from diesel as harvest stalls in the rain
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: WTI settled $91.26 Friday, down 1.5%, while Dated Brent physical barrels reportedly cleared $120 the same day as Hormuz tanker strikes (ongoing since the Iran war began) widen the crude-diesel split. That spread is why your diesel bill isn't following the crude headline down. Action: Diesel buyers: lock the next 30 days of on-farm fuel now; WTI at $91.26 says cheap, physical diesel markets say otherwise. • Crude Down, Diesel Up, Same Barrel • Harvest Stalls, Basis Stays Put Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-03

item.title: Crude drops 3.5% as grains grind higher on no news
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn held $5.00 flat, beans ticked up to $12.77, and crude fell 3.5% to $89.37 on Gulf export flow that's actually working this time. That's the real story today: oil giving back the fear premium while grains just sit there, unbothered. Action: Crude under $89.37 and falling: lock any diesel needs now, this Gulf-flow story isn't done unwinding. • Crude Gives Back More Ground • Grains Sit On Their Hands • Cattle Firm, Cull Cows Don't Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-02

item.title: Corn runs 1.1% ahead of stocks, crude up on Gulf flows
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn's up 5 cents to $5.04, Chicago wheat added 8 cents to $6.80, and crude ran 3.3% to $92.08, all three moving before Quarterly Stocks even prints at 11 CT. That's not reaction, that's positioning, and positioning ahead of a Stocks report is a bet, not a read. Action: Unpriced corn in the bin: a close above $5.09 says the Stocks positioning was real, price another 10% there. • Grains Run Ahead Of Stocks • Crude Runs On Gulf Flow Reports Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-01

item.title: Grains tick higher ahead of stocks data at 11 CT
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn's up a quarter-cent shy of $5.25, beans up a nickel-plus to $13.03, and none of it means much with Quarterly Grain Stocks landing at 11 CT. Nobody's positioning hard into a report that could move old-crop supply pictures either way. Every bushel priced this morning got priced without knowing what USDA knows. Action: Nothing to do at $5.25 corn ahead of Grain Stocks; a settle above $5.29 on the data is the first reason to move. • Grains Wait On Stocks • Cattle Cycle Turns, Slowly • Crude Holds The Iran Bid Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-30

item.title: Crude pulls back 2.1% as Yanbu reopens
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: WTI settled $92.12, down 2.1%, the first real give-back after two days running toward $96 on Iran-Hormuz fear. Saudi Arabia just restarted loadings at Yanbu on the Red Sea after the East-West pipeline came back partial, and that's a supply story beating a fear story today. Action: Diesel buyers: WTI at **$92.12** is the cheapest print in three sessions; lock the next fuel load now before any bounce back to $94. • Crude Gives Back The Fear Premium • Grains Drift On Empty China Wires Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-29

item.title: Crude runs to $96 as beans slip again
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Crude added 2.3% to $96.13 on Iran war-fear headlines out of the UN General Assembly, the same Hormuz cycle that's flared and cooled twice since April, and diesel-hungry harvest crews are the ones who pay for it. Action: Diesel-dependent harvest budgets: crude above $96.13 and running, lock fuel needs now rather than wait for a pullback that may not come. • Crude Runs On Iran Fear • Beans Slip On Empty China News Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-28

item.title: Grains climb Friday, cattle stall before COF week
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn closed Friday at $5.29, up 1.7% on the week's last session, and wheat gained 1.8% to $7.04 on nothing more than a bearish China trade story running out of sellers. item.title: Grains sit still, cattle slip again before COF
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn eased to $5.17, beans barely moved at $13.04, and neither market gave you a reason to do anything today. Action: Live cattle at $218.95: nothing to do ahead of Cattle on Feed at 2:00 PM CT, but a close under $216.50 is the next sell. • Cattle Slips Again, Report Looms • Grains Stay Parked Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-25

item.title: Crude runs to $93 as Hormuz traffic stays thin
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Crude added 2.1% to $93.19 and it isn't demand talking, it's one vessel crossing the Strait of Hormuz Wednesday, stuck below the 10-day average with the Iran-Hormuz cycle still refusing to fully unwind. Action: Lock diesel needs now; a close above $6.55 on the rack price is the next reason to pre-buy fall fuel, not wait. • Crude Runs On Thin Hormuz Traffic • Grains Give Back More Ground • Cattle Grind Higher Again Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-24

item.title: Grains give back the China pop ahead of Xi summit
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn settled $5.29, down 3½ cents, wheat down a penny and three-quarters, both giving back Monday's China-hope pop before Thursday's Trump-Xi summit even opens. Cattle fell 0.8% to $219.35 the day after a 2.4% jump on record-low placements, that's real profit-taking, not a reversal of the placements story. Action: Corn: no action above $5.29, but a settle below $5.27 says the China pop is fully unwound, price the next 10%. • Grains Fade The Summit Pop • Cattle Cool After Placement Pop Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-23

item.title: Corn rallies on China hopes; cattle jump 2.4%
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn ran 15 cents to three-week highs and beans gained 24 cents overnight on fresh hope for a US-China trade deal, but both gave it back into the close, corn settling $5.38 and beans $13.19, both down on the day. Cattle didn't fade: $221.15, up 2.4% on record low placements. Action: Live cattle at $221.15: nothing to sell into a 2.4% up day off record low placements, hold for $222 confirmation. • Grains Fade The China Pop • Cattle Ignore The Grain Fade • Crude Reverses On Iran Hope Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-22

item.title: Beans flat, diesel at $6.50, crude breaks on Iran thaw
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Soybeans sit at $13.10, off a penny and a half, still waiting on Xi. Meanwhile diesel crossed $6.50 a gallon this weekend, a record, while crude fell to $92.97 on Iran diplomacy hopes: two energy stories moving in opposite directions on the same headline. Action: Diesel at $6.50/gallon: lock harvest fuel needs now, don't wait for crude's Iran-talk dip to reach the pump. • Diesel Record, Crude Breaks • Beans Wait On Xi Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-21
